item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B is narrowly scoped and implements the frozen contract directly; Candidate A introduces prohibited API and retry-layer changes and duplicates FilesService.Add behavior.","reasons":["B adds exactly the requested Upload signature, validates filename/content before encoding, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and delegates to FilesService.Add so existing options, request construction, decoding, and errors remain centralized.","B’s tests cover multipart field/name/content, retrying non-seekable streamed content after a 429, pre-request validation, and source-reader error propagation.","A adds multiple association options and NewFileWithFields machinery despite the explicit prohibition on association fields and requirement to keep FilesOption behavior unchanged.","A bypasses FilesService.Add and reproduces its request/response logic inside Upload, violating the required routing and creating duplicate maintenance paths with potentially divergent semantics—including a new missing-data error behavior for Upload alone—not via Add as contracted clearly explicitly required centralized decoding/error handling stay in one place standardized existing behavior consistency issue significant review concern major contract breach concrete visible code evidence difference meaningful preference B strongly superior directly compliant implementation concise idiomatic reuse established helper exact scope disciplined test coverage complete no unrelated modifications. Candidate A also refactors RawClient body ownership, seek handling, content length, retry behavior, README, and changelog—changes explicitly outside scope and potentially API-semantic changes across Files.Update, Raw.Do, and other uploads."],"risks_a":["The new adoptRequestBody closes-over and reuses one shared io.Seeker for retries, broadening concurrency and lifecycle risks across all Raw.Do callers.","Replacing an empty seekable body with http.NoBody changes the supplied-body semantics, while wrapping caller closers changes established transport ownership behavior.","A does not visibly test Upload source-reader failure propagation, one of the contract’s named cases."],"risks_b":["The retry test validates the multipart payload only on the retried attempt rather than comparing both attempts, though it still demonstrates successful replay of streamed input.","Errors from multipartbody.NewFile are returned without additional Upload-specific context, but this preserves underlying source-reader failures and matches the narrow contract."]}
